title: USGS: rock ages are read from parent and daughter isotopes
summary: A USGS geologic-time page says parent isotopes decay to daughter isotopes at a predictable rate, and that the ratio is used to calculate the age of the rock.
body: The USGS page "Graphical Representation of Geologic Time," last updated 25 March 2008, says Earth is very old, 4.5 billion years or more according to recent estimates on that page. It says rocks that were once molten contain radioactive elements whose isotopes provide an atomic clock. It says parent isotopes decay at a predictable rate to form daughter isotopes, and that the age of these rocks can be calculated from the relative amounts of parent and daughter isotopes. It says studies of rock layers, fossils, and those ages together attest to a very old Earth. A different USGS page already stores a more precise age figure. This card is the dating method and the round estimate this page states.
